title: Winning Chez Florence in 1946 with a half-Black, half-white band
summary: Competing with Combelle and Rostand, Briggs got the job on condition that half the band be Black and half white, all French; after a slow first month the place filled up and he stayed until 1950.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, there were quite a few of us trying to get the same job at Chez Florence's. Hubert Rostand, my friend, and Combelle --
Combelle. No, Barelli had his job on -- he was Carreas on the Rue Pierre Charon, Champs d'Elysees Nord.
But, Combelle, and certain others were all trying to get Chez Florence's because it was a good job.
And when I finally got it, they told me, they said, 'You can have the job, but we must have half colored and half white.'

I said, 'Okay.' 'Half colored and half white, but they must all be French.' 'Except you'. 'They must all be French.' I said, 'Okay'. After all, there was nothing I could do. I said -- see, I went around, and I finally got them the -- the French boys, four colored and four Europeans, and we formed an orchestra, and there was no audition or anything. They just said, 'We will give you a month's contract, and if everything is okay, then --' Well, it so happened that after a month, we didn't have very many people in the place. It was -- we opened the end of February, the end of February for the smart set, that either in the summer was in the South of France or somewhere else, Monte Carlo --

So, the first month -- after the first month, the managing director said to me -- I said to him, "Well, what's going to happen." He said, "Well, you'll continue. You have another month." I said, "No, I'll have two more months to make it three months. Otherwise I finish this evening and we're finished." So he said, "Okay". Within fifteen days, you could hardly move in the place.

Then he wanted me to sign forever. But I said, "No". So, we continued that way. Don't need any contract. I said, "The contract is the public. That's the contract." "As long as the place kept on going, there's no problem." And then I had two orchestras up, worked both of them. My orchestra and a small orchestra, six. And we kept going. I stayed with Chez Florence's until the end
